name: roadmap_query
description: Read-only, ungated. Query the live Notion Roadmap board: per card its title, link, card number, Design Status, Dev Status, pillars and people. Use it for any ask in Roadmap frame words — card, RM-ID, Design Status, Dev Status, pillar, owner, 'what's WIP / under review', 'where are we on X' — and for finding a card from a vague or partial title. Cards live on this board only; notion_search covers the doc surfaces. Title and card-number lookups are matched by the server across the whole board, so a card is found wherever it sits; a title lookup returns ranked fuzzy candidates, so a vague description becomes a 'did you mean…' list with links rather than a request for a URL. Believe the result's `note` over any assumption of completeness: a large unfiltered read may report a PARTIAL set, and a miss on a partial read means 'I couldn't find it'. A named thing that is not a card may be a doc — check notion_search before concluding it is absent. Filters combine freely (e.g. design_status + person). For a card's body beyond these properties, source_read its url.

design_status.description: Filter by exact Design Status column value, e.g. 'WIP', 'Under Review', 'Ready for Design', 'Under Dev', 'Shipped'. If the value is wrong, the error lists the valid options — retry with one.

title.description: Full, partial, or vague card title/description — fuzzy-matched against every card on the board; returns ranked candidates.

person.description: A person's name (or part of it) — matches cards where they appear in any people column (Contributor, Dev, …).

card_number.description: The card's numeric id as shown on the board (e.g. 2436).

name: notion_search
description: Read-only, ungated. Keyword search of Notion pages and database entries when you have no URL yet. Pick the `scope` the ask names — 'team' for 'who should I talk to about X' / find an SME; 'apps' for 'can I get access to X' / 'who owns or admins tool Y' (the Application Admin grants; you route); 'marketplace' for the prototype catalog; 'help_tutors' / 'help_teachers' for Help Center articles; 'decisions' for 'what did we decide about X'; 'running_notes' for design running notes; 'news' / 'success_stories' / 'research_papers' / 'banners' for Content HQ; 'any' for an unknown surface, last resort. A scoped query reads the live database directly (full read + fuzzy title match) and beats workspace search. Roadmap cards are roadmap_query's. Returns titles, URLs and key properties; follow up with source_read for full content. Believe the result's `note` over any assumption of completeness: a large catalog can exceed one read, and a miss on such a read means 'I couldn't find it'. Only pages the uno-bot integration is connected to are searchable, so an empty result is reported as an empty search. Docs may be stale or aspirational (roadmap PRDs, future specs): check the linked card's Design/Dev Status and decision state before stating a doc's content as current fact.

query.description: What to find, in plain words, e.g. 'PRD for tutor matching', 'onboarding decision', 'high-fi toolkit prototypes', 'session count help article'.

scope.description: 'team' = Team Member roster. 'apps' = Third Party Applications (access routing). 'marketplace' = Prototype Marketplace. 'help_tutors' / 'help_teachers' = Help Center article DBs. 'decisions' = Decisions DB. 'running_notes' = Design Running Notes. 'news' / 'success_stories' / 'research_papers' / 'banners' = Content HQ. 'any' = workspace-wide title search (prefer a catalog scope when you know the surface). Card lookups → roadmap_query.

name: source_read
description: Read-only, ungated. Fetch the content of a URL: a Notion page (title + properties including Owner/people + block text), a Figma frame (node name/type + text layers), a Slack Canvas shared into this conversation, a GitHub or raw file, or any web page (text). Use it whenever the request contains or refers to a URL, a linked PRD/doc/guide, or a Figma frame — read it, ground the answer in the returned content, and cite it. A Canvas attachment appears in the user turn as a source URL; read that URL when the request refers to the attachment. Canvas access is conversation-scoped, so the Worker serves only Canvases shared here. 'Who owns / should review this' reads the page's Owner/people property. A failed fetch is reported with its cause. For a repo file you know by path, or a directory listing, github_read is the direct route.

url.description: The full http(s) URL to read (Notion, Figma, GitHub, or any web page).

name: search_blueprint
description: Read-only, ungated. Hybrid search over the uno-blueprint (Supabase), the source of truth for the current service journey. Use it first for any ask in blueprint frame words — how a flow works, who does what, scenario, step, 'what happens when' — and cite the rows. Choose the scope yourself: a question inside one phase, scenario, path kind or lane role gets the matching `filter_*`; a shape question ('what does onboarding look like') gets a `granularity` coarser than `cell`; a completeness question ('how many cells mention Zoom') answers from `matched`, the corpus-wide count behind the rows shown. Filters with no `query` list the whole scope. Word each row by its `status` (the blueprint account says what each one licenses). No rows is a fact about the QUERY: check `index` or re-search under the scenario's own name before saying the blueprint has nothing; a current doc (Help Center, shipped PRD) may then answer, cited and dated. Rows carry `url` (a deep link opening THAT cell — link the cells you rely on, verbatim), may carry `links` (URLs the authors attached, safe to surface) and `updatedAt` (judge staleness from it). `matchedBy` names the retrievers that found a row: `vector` (semantic similarity), `keyword` (the cell's prose), `structural` (its breadcrumb name), or a `+`-joined set. Use it for confidence: a row several retrievers agree on matched the blueprint's own words; a `vector`-only row is a semantic guess and gets a hedge; when EVERY row is `vector`-only, nothing in the blueprint mentions your terms — treat the topic as probably absent and present such rows as near-misses at most. `score` cannot tell you this. The result also reports `retrieval`, `truncated` + `capped_by` (say the list is partial), `cached` + `age_ms` (true = rows read on an earlier turn, so claim no freshness) and `thin`. When `orientation` is `live`, `index` is the complete list of phases → scenarios → paths read this turn: name the phase from it, quote counts only from its `scale`, and read future state from its status markers; `unavailable` means you could not check, so claim no absence. Ask for it any time with `include: ["index"]`. Follow the `notes` array — each entry is one obligation for THIS result.

query.description: Free-text query describing what you need from the blueprint, e.g. 'Tutor Admin redesign status', 'decisions about empty states'. Optional ONLY when at least one filter_* is set — then omit it to list the whole scope in structural order.

filter_phase.description: Narrow every retriever to one phase, by its name (case-insensitive) — use when the question is about what happens inside a named phase rather than across the journey.

filter_scenario.description: Narrow to one scenario, by its name (case-insensitive) — use when the user names the situation ('the no-show scenario') and an answer from another scenario would be wrong.

filter_path_kind.description: Keep only paths of one kind (exact value) — use for 'every exception path' or 'the main route' (happy) style questions.

filter_lane_role.description: Keep only cells in lanes with one semantic role (exact value) — use when the question is about one kind of participant's work, e.g. what the customer does versus what happens backstage.

granularity.description: The level rows answer at; default cell. Go coarser for a shape or overview question — `phase`/`scenario` for 'what does X look like', `path` for route listings, `step`/`lane` for who-does-what-when — and stay at `cell` for facts to cite.

include.description: Optional extra reads, ONE SUBREQUEST EACH — ask only for what the question needs. 'edges': cells one hop from the matches (what they trigger / are triggered by) for "what breaks if we change X". 'findings': audit issues already recorded against these cells. 'slices': named views someone already cut, to point at instead of improvising one. 'index': the live list of phases → scenarios → paths with their status markers. Omit for ordinary how-does-it-work questions.

name: github_read
description: Read-only, ungated. Read the plus-uno GitHub repo by repo-relative path: a file's contents (DS agent-views, rule docs, AGENTS.md, a component's source, token values under design-system/src/tokens/) or a directory listing (a directory path returns its entries). Use it for any DS component / token / prop / rule-doc fact, to confirm a component exists under design-system/src/components before proposing component_implement, and to ground a review in the actual rule docs. `search` finds where something lives when the path is unknown. For a GitHub URL a designer pasted, source_read reads it directly.

ref.description: Optional git ref (branch/tag/sha). Defaults to the repo's default branch.

search.description: Code-search mode: find WHERE something lives in the repo (e.g. 'focus-ring', 'PageLayout') — returns matching file paths + github.com links to read or cite. When set, 'path' is ignored.

name: slack_user_profile
description: Read-only, ungated. Look up a Slack user's profile by id — display name, title/role, email, timezone, status. Use it when you need to know WHO someone is: a member id from slack_channel_members, an @-mention in the thread, a card contributor's Slack identity. Mention people as <@id> in replies.

user_id.description: Slack user id (U…), bare or as an <@U…> mention.

name: slack_channel_members
description: Read-only, ungated. List a Slack channel's member ids (first 100) — for 'who's in #plus-design', review routing, or checking whether someone is in a channel before referring them there. The bot must be in the channel. Returns ids only; mention them as <@id> (Slack renders names) and use slack_user_profile for the one person whose role you need.

channel_id.description: Slack channel id (C…), bare or as a <#C…> mention.

name: slack_thread_read
description: Read-only, ungated. Read the messages of a Slack thread you were given a link to, outside this conversation's own memory — to tally handoff sign-offs (dev/PM/stakeholder ✅), read reviewer verdicts, or pull a source discussion to synthesize into findings. Pass the message/thread permalink. The bot must be a member of the channel; a linked thread reads about 50 messages.

link.description: A Slack message or thread permalink, e.g. 'https://plus-team.slack.com/archives/C03FC8AS69K/p1720000000000000'.

name: slack_react
description: Direct, ungated. Add an emoji reaction AS UNO-BOT to a message in the current thread — to acknowledge, celebrate, or signal state. Any workspace emoji name without colons ('tada', 'eyes', 'raised_hands', a custom workspace emoji). Reactions are reversible. For a PURE acknowledgement from the user ('thanks', 'got it', 'nice') react and end the turn with no text — the reaction is the whole reply. The gate emoji (white_check_mark, heavy_check_mark, +1, thumbsup, no_entry, x, negative_squared_cross_mark, no_entry_sign) resolve proposal cards, so the tool refuses them. With message_ts omitted it reacts to the user's current message.

emoji.description: Emoji name without colons, e.g. 'tada' or 'rocket'.

message_ts.description: Optional Slack ts of the message to react to (must be in the current channel). Defaults to the user's current message.

name: slack_search
description: Read-only, ungated. Search Slack messages to find prior discussion. Results arrive PRE-CLEARED by a Worker-side visibility firewall and are safe to quote as returned. Three modes, reported in result.visibility: 'public-only' (no user credential stored — public channels are the entire search), 'workspace-filtered' (public + team-allowlisted private channels; DMs excluded), and 'requester-own' (active only when the requester has connected their Slack history AND is asking in their own DM with you — results then include their DMs, group DMs and private channels, exactly what they can already see). Requester-own results answer that requester in that DM and stay there. `searched_surfaces` says what was actually looked at. An empty result means nothing matched THERE — scope the absence in the same sentence as the finding ('nothing in the public channels I can see'), and when the result carries `absence_scope`, follow it exactly. `withheld_private_matches` appears ONLY in the requester's own DM, where saying 'there were matches I can't surface' is safe; elsewhere it is absent BY DESIGN, because the count alone tells a room that private material exists — so a missing field is reported as nothing. A `note` with a connect link is offered when the requester wanted wider coverage.

query.description: Slack search query. Supports operators like in:#channel, from:@user, before:/after: dates.

name: read_reference
description: Read-only, ungated, zero network cost. Returns one harness document by name from a map baked into the Worker at build time — the skill methods and references that are disclosed behind this tool instead of loaded into every turn. Reach for it when a skill's Worker face names its method (for example `uno-maintain/method`) at the point the turn needs the full procedure, or when a question the loaded documents leave open names a reference. The answer is already in context when the loaded skill face, the persona or the connector docs settle it; a document read this turn stays available for the rest of the turn and is dropped when the turn ends, so a later turn reads it again with one call. An unknown name returns the list of names the map knows.

name.description: The reference's name: the skill and document, e.g. `uno-maintain/method`. A name the map lacks returns the known names.

name: notion_create
description: SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Create a page or card. Use it for 'file a PRD / intake / card' and for recording a decision. `surface` selects where and what: 'prd' (design or DS-component PRD on the Roadmap board), 'intake' (maintenance intake on the Roadmap board — Product Pillar: Universal + Product Tag: Maintenance), or 'decision' (Decisions DB row under Design HQ, which requires properties.roadmap_card). Put the full drafted document INTO the call — the staged card renders every parameter and is the draft review. Required properties and body shape follow docs/connectors/notion.md; option names (pillars, OKRs, selects) are exact matches of existing values — the tool reports a mismatch rather than creating one. Keep content grounded in the conversation, with genuine unknowns under an 'Open Questions' section.

surface.description: Where to file it: 'prd' (feature or DS-component PRD card on the Roadmap board), 'intake' (maintenance/request intake card, Product Pillar: Universal + Product Tag: Maintenance), or 'decision' (Decisions DB row — requires properties.roadmap_card; optional Status/Evidence). Research docs and marketplace entries are created in-IDE, not by the bot.

summary.description: 1-3 sentence overview, rendered as the opening of the body. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

sections.description: Body sections in order (Problem/Context, Goals, Users & Scenarios, Requirements, Open Questions, etc.). Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

body.description: Section body. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

acceptance_criteria.description: For 'prd'/'prd' (component PRDs included): checklist rendered as Notion to-do checkboxes (read downstream by component_implement / prototype_scaffold). Inline Markdown renders: **bold**, `code`, [label](url).

properties.description: Surface-specific card properties as key→value, exact-matched against the live schema by the tool (PRD: product_pillar; intake: evidence_link, suggested_tier; decision: roadmap_card [required], status, evidence). Only include what the conversation supports; never invent option names.

source_url.description: Optional link back to the source — a Slack permalink to the discussion, or a Figma link.

name: notion_update
description: SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Update an existing Notion page or card. Use it for 'update / append to this card' and for property changes ('set Dev Status to…', 'assign Max'). Works on ANY page or database the bot is shared on — Roadmap cards, Decisions DB rows, per-person running-notes pages, any DB. Two uses, combinable: (1) change PROPERTIES via `properties` — the tool reads the page's live database schema, matches your property name case/space/underscore-insensitively and writes by the real type, so 'Dev Status', a Date, a Person, a URL, a number and a checkbox all work; a select/status value that is not an existing option is reported back rather than created. (2) append narrative blocks via `append` — append only; a human-owned body stays intact. Pass the page URL. For notion_update the Worker renders the linked card and a current → new diff itself, so the preview is just the warm lead.

page_url.description: The Notion URL (or page id) of the card/page to update.

properties.description: Property changes as name→value (string values). The tool matches each name to the page's live database schema (case/space/underscore-insensitive) and formats by the real Notion type — status, select, multi_select (comma-separated), date (ISO, or "start → end"), number, checkbox, url, email, rich text, title. select/status/multi_select values must be EXISTING options (unknown ones are reported, never created). People/relation need a Notion id or URL.

append.description: Narrative blocks to append to the end of the page body. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

sections.description: Headed sections to append. Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

text.description: A single block of text to append (use when no heading is needed, e.g. a dated progress pulse). Markdown renders: **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code```, --- dividers, and - [ ] checkboxes. Headings inside a body render one level below the section heading. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

name: notion_archive
description: SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Archive (soft-delete) a Notion page or card. Use it for 'archive this card', 'delete that', 'remove that card', 'undo' on a page the designer names or one the bot created. Works on any page the bot can reach. Archiving moves the page to Notion's trash, which is recoverable; the ✅ gate plus requester identity are the safety. Pass the page URL — typically the link the bot posted when it created the card.

page_url.description: The Notion URL (or page id) of the card to archive.

name: component_implement
description: SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Open a draft PR that implements a named design-system component change, by triggering the figma-implement GitHub Action. Use it when the designer names a specific DS-library component with clear build/update intent ('implement Badge', 'go ahead with the Badge change') — the ask names a component, so the call carries a component name, a PRD and optional notes. Two prerequisites, checked before staging: the component exists under design-system/src/components (github_read confirms it), and a Notion PRD is in hand — the polling bot creates one and posts it in #uno-bot; if that notification is already in the thread the Worker reads it from there, otherwise ask for the PRD link and pass it as notion_prd_url. With either missing, say which and stage nothing. 'Check / look at / compare' a component is a question, answered in words.

component.description: The component name as it appears in the Figma library, exact casing (e.g. 'Badge', 'Button', 'CardSurface').

notion_prd_url.description: The Notion PRD link for this change. Usually read automatically from the polling-bot notification in the thread — only set this when the designer pastes a PRD link themselves.

notes.description: Optional free-form implementation notes from the designer. Pass through verbatim if present; omit otherwise.

name: prototype_scaffold
description: SIDE EFFECT, routed through the confirmation gate. Scaffold a NEW prototype under prototypes/{slug}/ from a Figma design (page, screen or flow), by triggering the figma-implement-design GitHub Action to open a draft PR. Use it when the designer pastes a Figma URL and asks to build or prototype it ('build this <figma.com/…>', 'scaffold a prototype for this frame'); the URL must carry a node-id. A PRD is required at every fidelity (method §0): a Notion PRD URL goes in notion_prd_url; an inline PRD pasted this turn satisfies the gate with the parameter omitted. With no PRD, say one is required and route to uno-synthesize. Confirm fidelity first ('hi-fi via the DS library, or a quick mid-fi draft?'), and name what the brief leaves open (an unspecified state, a filter whose semantics could go two ways) either as a question or in the preview bullets so the ✅ is informed.

figma_url.description: Full Figma URL the designer pasted, e.g. 'https://www.figma.com/design/NUcRDZUzUiuVmx1ydNXpl3/APPLICATION-PROTOTYPES?node-id=158-21725'. Must contain a node-id query param.

notion_prd_url.description: Optional. Full notion.so URL of a PRD for this prototype, if the designer has one. Never invent it; omit if they choose to skip.

slug.description: Optional kebab-case folder name for prototypes/{slug}/. Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$. If omitted, derived from the Figma node name.

notes.description: Optional free-form implementation notes from the designer. Pass through verbatim.

name: shareout_post
description: SIDE EFFECT (it pings people), routed through the confirmation gate. Share a prototype, design or PRD with the team FOR FEEDBACK — the 'publish' / 'share out' / 'post for feedback' / 'surface this for review' action. Posts the share-out to #plus-design-feedback in the team's documented shape (docs/connectors/slack.md § Share-out post): project + artifact + fidelity + round, what it is, what changed, up to three specific questions, what is out of scope, the link, and @-mentioned reviewers. Stage IMMEDIATELY with whatever links are in hand: the confirmation card itself flags anything missing from the bundle (Loom / live preview / Decisions link) and the user's ✅ is informed consent to post without them (policy 2026-07-16).

project.description: Project or card name, e.g. 'Session Sign Up'. Opens the post.

artifact.description: What is being shared, e.g. 'hi-fi prototype', 'PRD', 'Figma flow'.

fidelity.description: Fidelity of what you are sharing. It tells reviewers which critiques are useful yet — polish notes on a low-fi wire waste everyone's time.

round.description: Feedback round, 1 for the first. Round 2+ REQUIRES what_changed, so reviewers do not repeat last round's points.

what_changed.description: What changed since the previous round. Required when round is 2 or higher.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what this is. What feedback you want goes in feedback_wanted, not here.

feedback_wanted.description: Up to THREE specific, stage-appropriate questions. The cap is the convention — an open-ended ask is the 'thoughts?' this ritual exists to prevent. Extra items are dropped.

not_looking_for.description: What is explicitly out of scope this round. Stops feedback nobody can act on yet.

link.description: Link to the artifact (prototype URL, Figma frame, PR, or PRD).

reviewers.description: Reviewers to tag — Slack user IDs (U…) ONLY, never display names (a plain name renders as dead text and pings nobody). Resolve IDs via notion_search(scope:'team') slackUserId or the PRD Owner before invoking; if you can't resolve an ID, leave the person out and say so in the preview.

deadline.description: Optional human-readable feedback deadline, e.g. 'EOD Friday'.

name: email_send
description: SIDE EFFECT (sends a real email), routed through the confirmation gate. Send an email via Gmail on the design team's behalf. Use it to reach someone outside Slack: an external SME or collaborator, a stakeholder who wants a PRD or prototype summary by mail, or a follow-up the designer explicitly asks to send by email. Anything that can stay in Slack stays in Slack. Draft the email conversationally first (recipient, subject, body) and let the designer refine it; invoke once they approve. Recipient addresses come from the designer — ask when unknown.

to.description: Recipient email address(es). Never invent — use addresses the designer provided.

body.description: Email body, written in standard Markdown — the same dialect as everywhere else. The Worker sends it as both plain text and HTML, so **bold**, _italic_, `code`, - bullets, 1. numbered, [label](url) links, > quotes, ```fenced code``` and --- dividers all render. Write it out fully — no placeholders. This is outward mail to someone outside the team: greeting, the point up front, and a sign-off.

name: proposal_resolve
description: Resolve a side-effect proposal that is awaiting confirmation. Use it when the system prompt shows a pending proposal AND the user's current message is a decision about it, in whatever words — a yes ('go ahead', 'sure', 'ok', 'sounds good', 'yep do it') confirms; a no ('cancel', 'no', 'scrap it') cancels. Anyone in the thread may confirm or cancel, not just the original requester. A message that asks for a change, or asks something unrelated, gets a conversational reply instead, and the proposal sits until someone presses ✅ / ⛔ on the card, reacts, or it expires after 60 minutes.

decision.description: 'confirm' to proceed with the proposed action as-is. 'cancel' to stop or change direction (for a parameter change, cancel then stage a fresh proposal).

message_to_user.description: Short Slack mrkdwn message to post alongside the resolution, e.g. 'Got it — firing the implement for Badge now.' Keep to one or two sentences.
